## Summary

Concretum analyzed **more than 1,500 trades from a futures trend program** to interrogate the single most praised characteristic of CTA funds: **positive skew** — the fat-right-tail payoff profile ("lose small often, win big occasionally") that trend following's marketing rests on. Their finding, per the truncated teaser: the positive asymmetry often credited to trend following **"isn't quite what"** [text cut] — i.e., something about the conventional story doesn't survive contact with the trade data. The actual punchline is in the unlinked full piece; the attached chart presumably shows the trade-level distribution evidence.

## Why it matters

- **This stress-tests the exact prior our TF cluster rests on.** The vault's trend-following replications ([[2026-08-29-three-simple-ma-atr-systems]], [[2026-08-30-ignis-trend-following-realtest]], [[2026-10-06-junglerockres-turtle-hurst-gate]]) are evaluated mostly on aggregate stats (CAGR/Sharpe/drawdown). If skew is weaker, more fragile, or more concentrated than advertised, trade-level distribution checks belong in every replication's acceptance criteria — not just aggregate performance.
- **Right evidentiary shape:** trade-level analysis of 1,500+ real trades from an actual futures program beats narrative claims about "CTA skew" hands down. Plausible findings this could be: skew driven by a handful of outlier trades (removing top-1% collapses the asymmetry), skew varying wildly by market regime, or position-sizing (vol targeting) manufacturing the skew rather than the signal itself.
- **Same shop as [[2026-09-18-concretum-rebalancing-flows-alpha]]** — Concretum (Carlo Zarattini & co.) publish SSRN-grade, methodology-heavy work; a "your favorite property is weaker than you think" headline from them is a genuine research finding, not engagement bait.
- **Skepticism gates:** (1) the finding itself is truncated mid-sentence — do not assume the skew is *absent*, only that it's *not what it's claimed to be*; (2) one program, 1,500+ trades — single-sample; a different futures book (markets traded, sizing scheme) could tell a different story; (3) "futures trend program" is unidentified in the tweet — whose program, what period; (4) chart unOCRed; (5) full article not yet located.
- **Actionable:** locate the full piece (concretumgroup.com publications / their SSRN cluster), OCR the chart, and add a trade-level skew check (P&L histogram, top-decile trade contribution) to the TF replication checklist.
